ToolRegistry.invoke at packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolRegistry.ts:231-236 returns the generic validation error; packages/core/src/model/toolSchemaValidation.ts:141-142 reports only the rejected key. Reproducer: from this worktree run node_modules/.bin/tsx /tmp/l4-useitem-unknown-args.mts. For real magic-item:rope-of-entanglement / entangle-creature, args {transitionOutome:'failure'} returns exactly 'use_item arguments failed schema validation: args.args.transitionOutome is not allowed', without 'transitionOutcome, transitionTo'. Likewise control-plus-unknown returns only 'args.args.unknownPredicate is not allowed'; real magic-item:bag-of-tricks / pull-fuzzy-object with {unknown:true} does not say that the operation takes no args. The direct useItemTool.run path does list accepted names, so this is a producer/consumer discrepancy, not a missing validator altogether. New tests itemUseArgsRefusal.test.ts:119-147 check only the rejected name on registry calls; :151-180 assert accepted-key wording only while bypassing that registry. Sibling class: every registry-rejected unknown args property, on transition, fixed-cost and variable-cost operations. No SRD page governs this software diagnostic requirement; source context for the Rope outcome remains p.241, 'The target must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or become restrained.' Severity is NON-MATERIAL: refusal, action budget, canonical state and RNG safety work; the missing information affects the stated recovery/error contract only. Owner: use_item boundary (.16.10.2 / integrating parent). Closure: make registry-path unknown-argument refusals name the actual selected operation's accepted keys, retaining schema refusal and defaults. Permanent evidence should be one generalized registry-level diagnostic invariant over a transition and a no-args operation; that is proportionate to an error-message contract and prevents the bypass-only tests from hiding it. Under Findings discipline this accepted finding still requires repair before PR approval; NON-MATERIAL is not permission to defer it, and this review does not publish APPROVED.
S2 — L4-F1 MATERIAL FAILURE CLASS REPAIRED in the in-force population. Inspected useItem consumption/credit issuance, destroyInventoryItem, receipt/id retirement, grant validation/redemption, destroyed-source serialization and cleanup consumer. inventoryLifecycle.ts:76-83 preserves credits only when a consumption receipt retires the id; other destruction retains its existing voiding behavior. activeEffects.ts:4334-4397 admits the oldest or named open credit on the destroyed-source path, clears receipt payment when a credit pays, and refuses already-redeemed receipts and invalid named credits. Receipt and credit redemption remain in the effect-insert transaction (:5677-5691). sourceDestroyedAt is separately retained and serialized at :5655-5657, so credit-paid post-consumption effects are born tombstoned rather than trying to schedule a deleted item's cooldown. Source independently checked with pdftotext from the vendored SRD PDF p.220: 'When you use an action to break the gem, an elemental is summoned as if you had cast the conjure elemental spell, and the gem’s magic is lost.' Table confirms all four elemental/gem identities. Re-ran original /tmp/l4-gem-conservation.mts: all four colors at quantity 2 and 3 retain n-1 credits after final consumption and bind n times. The permanent generalized conservation test covers bind-as-you-go and use-all-then-bind, n+1 refusal, exhausted entitlements, id retirement and a new unused stack's inability to redeem old rights. Independent /tmp/pr702-review.mts additionally redeems two explicitly named credits in reverse order after consuming three gems, refuses unknown and duplicate credit ids without DB mutation, redeems the final receipt, and asserts all three item_grant_json bindings carry the consumed timestamp as sourceDestroyedAt.
